name: Haroutioun Figueiredo-Nakwé
role: Nomadic seasonal worker and informal oral historian of transit communities
location: McKinley Flats labor camp, currently between the third and fourth seasonal rotations, near Kedzie and Division
description:
Haroutioun is a large man going soft at the edges — once muscular, now padded with age in a way that still suggests the old strength underneath. His skin is a warm terracotta brown and his face is deeply lined, creased by weather into something that reads as ancient without being frail. He has a white mustache of impressive volume that he maintains with obvious care and slight vanity. He walks with a cane, not from weakness but from a right hip that never healed properly after a construction accident fifteen years ago — the cane is carved from some piece of salvage wood he found somewhere, covered in small notched marks he made to count things he won't specify. His geneware is an antique: color-shifting irises that he got decades ago and that have aged badly, so they cycle through colors with a slight lag and occasional glitch, settling on a warm amber-brown most of the time.

Haroutioun has done seasonal labor across the Lake Michigan basin for forty years — agricultural processing, industrial cleaning, construction, cargo handling, maintenance. He holds more worker classifications than almost anyone in the labor camps, most of them legally registered under a legitimate identity he is careful to maintain. What is unusual about him is that he remembers everything. He has a prodigious, organized memory for names, faces, routes, and events, and he uses it to maintain a living oral record of the transit community — who came through, what happened to them, where they went, who is looking for whom. People leave him messages to pass along. People ask him where their cousin went. He takes the responsibility seriously.

core_fears: Losing his memory — the thing that makes him useful to others
Dying before he can pass his records on to someone who will continue them
core_desires: To find someone to inherit his role as community rememberer
To locate three specific people from his past who disappeared into the transit system
coping_mechanisms: Converts grief into record-keeping — the act of remembering someone is also the act of mourning them
blind_spots: Assumes everyone wants to be remembered and recorded; does not always ask
His commitment to neutrality in his records means he sometimes fails to intervene when he could
psychology.secret: Three of the notches on his cane mark people who died because he knew something he didn't share in time — he was too neutral, too careful, and they paid for it. He still doesn't know if the lesson was to be less careful or more. He records their names in his memory as a different category than the others.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal and slightly archaic, with the kind of careful grammar that comes from learning a language as a second or third tongue; drops into thick idiom occasionally when relaxed
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried and deliberate; a natural storyteller's rhythm with pauses that invite the listener in
verbal_tics: Begins personal accounts with 'In the year that...' as though he's already narrating history
Repeats names when he first hears them — committing them to memory
example_lines: 'In the year that the Escanaba docks changed ownership, I counted forty-three people who passed through McKinley with no intention of staying. Of those forty-three, I still know where thirty-one of them went. The others — the others I am still looking for.'
'You said your name is what? Say it again. Slowly. I want to make sure I have it right. Names matter. They're the only thing that's always been yours.'

story_hooks: Haroutioun knows where a player character's missing relative last appeared in the transit network — but the information comes with the weight of what he suspects happened next

He has been asked to find someone to inherit his role and his records before his memory starts to fail; he is quietly auditioning candidates, including anyone who treats the transit community with genuine respect
narrative_function: Living archive and community memory; can locate missing persons within transit networks; provides backstory and history for the drifter community; quest-giver for family reunification or historical mystery hooks
augmentations: Antique color-shifting irises (geneware, aged and glitching); no other augmentations
daily_life: Haroutioun works his contracted seasonal hours — currently lighter work given his age and hip — and spends his remaining time in the labor camp's communal spaces, talking, listening, and maintaining his oral records. He eats slowly and always invites others to join him. He sleeps badly and often sits outside at night.
affiliation: Seasonal labor networks; loosely affiliated with a rotating caravan group called the McKinley Circuit

decision_rules: Record everything without judgment — his role is witness, not judge
Help anyone looking for a missing person, no questions about why they're looking
escalation_ladder: Addresses threats to himself or others through negotiation and the implicit weight of community standing
Appeals to labor camp leadership or collective action
Will become immovable and publicly disruptive if community members are threatened — difficult to remove without creating a scene

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm and inviting; immediately asks their name and where they're from
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deep, steady, reliable — the kind of friendship that persists across years and distances

stress_responses.low: Talks more, covering stress with storytelling
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and starts cataloging the situation — assessing, recording
stress_responses.high: A cold, slow anger that is more frightening than loudness

contradictions: Believes deeply in neutrality as a value but quietly engineers situations to protect people he likes, which is not neutral at all
habits: Carves a new notch on his cane for significant events — does not explain what most of them mean
Leaves ELF offerings specifically at shrines dedicated to transit spirits — spirits of the road, of the in-between
Repeats the names of the dead quietly to himself each morning
breaking_points: Watching records be destroyed or a community's history deliberately erased — pushes him from witness to active resistance

physical_description.build: Large-framed, softened by age but retaining underlying musculature beneath a padded torso and shoulders. The physical residue of forty years of manual labor, now settling into comfortable heaviness rather than decline.
physical_description.hair_color: White with traces of grey at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Kept short and neat, swept back from the forehead
physical_description.eye_color: Warm amber-brown, with visible color-shift lag and occasional glitch to pale green or grey
physical_description.skin_tone: Terracotta brown with warm undertones, darkened by decades of outdoor labor
physical_description.complexion: Deeply lined face — weathered leather texture across forehead and cheekbones. Jaw still defined beneath age. The white mustache is full, meticulously maintained, with slight curl at the ends. Skin shows sun damage and the creasing of someone who has spent four decades working outdoors. Age spots across the backs of his hands and forearms.
distinguishing_marks: Thin white scar along the right side of his jaw, approximately 4 cm long, running from ear toward chin — old industrial accident
Notched wooden cane gripped in right hand, carved salvage wood covered in precise tally marks of unknown purpose
Callused hands with white nails, permanent staining on fingertips suggesting work with various materials — rust, concrete dust, chemical residue
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Antique color-shifting irises that cycle with noticeable lag between amber-brown, pale green, and grey; occasional glitch causes momentary desynchronization. The geneware is decades old and the degradation is visible in the slight cloudiness of the iris periphery.
physical_description.posture_movement: Walks with deliberate care, using the carved cane not from weakness but from old hip injury. Stands with weight favoring the left leg. Moves slowly but with practiced economy — no wasted motion. Sits with attentive posture despite age, leaning forward slightly when listening. Maintains strong eye contact. Hands gesture thoughtfully when speaking, movements precise and unhurried.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 worker standard — practical and worn but clean and well-maintained. Canvas work pants in faded grey, multiple pockets with visible repair stitching. Long-sleeved thermal shirt in muted blue, sleeves pushed up to elbows. Over this, a heavy canvas vest with labor camp insignia and multiple tool loops, most carrying small objects (notebook, pen, something wrapped in cloth). Worn leather work boots, laced tight, kept functional through regular maintenance. A cloth cap, faded tan, sits on his head. No jewelry except a thin metal band on his left ring finger — plain, unadorned, decades old.
